call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer: Design and demonstrate efficient thermal management and waste-heat reuse for server rooms in buildings or small local data centres. Operators need ways to reuse heat that would otherwise be rejected.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Show how better cooling and heat reuse can cut energy use, make waste heat useful and make performance data easier for others to access.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer: This suits building and small data-centre operators, cooling and controls suppliers, and local users of recovered heat. The group needs at least three independent grant recipients in different eligible countries, including one in a European Union Member State. Choose a lead from those recipients and include the organisations needed to integrate the heat recovery on site.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: Integrate commercially credible cooling and waste-heat recovery with the building or local heat user. The call expects a combined system and a business case for using the recovered heat.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer: Demonstrate heat recovery at existing server rooms or small data centres using 100–500 kilowatts, in both warm and cold climates. Integrate it with building controls and demonstrate a use for the heat on site or nearby.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: The pilots could change how small data centres use electricity and recover heat. The topic focuses on building systems and local heat use and sets out no transmission-operator work.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 15.75 million for small data-centre heat recovery. It expects 3 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 5.25 million per project. Different requests remain eligible.
- Funding form: Lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 201–203 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards small data-centre heat recovery. The rate is used to set the lump sum (a fixed grant paid for accepted work rather than reimbursing actual spending).
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for small data-centre heat recovery through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 15 September 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time. The technical proposal (Part B) is limited to 45 pages.
- Opening: 5 May 2027.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for small data-centre heat recovery.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The granting authority can restrict transfers of rights in the small data-centre heat-recovery results.
- Conditional requirement: Screen beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) control and use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing if covered satellite data or services are used.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
